transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Losing that gallery income has thrown me off so much that I feel like I’m not handling the money stress in a normal way anymore. It's gotten to the point where I'm worried it's starting to affect my day-to-day life, so a friend suggested I come talk to you.
Did these symptoms start only after the gallery income loss, or have you been feeling excessive worry about many different things for at least 6 months?

No, this is definitely a new thing that only started about a month ago, right after I found out the gallery was closing. I haven't been worrying like this for six months at all; it's a direct reaction to this sudden financial stress.
Since this stress started, has it been causing you significant problems at work, in relationships, or in daily activities, beyond what you would expect from the situation?

Yes, it really has been causing a lot of problems. I've been snapping at my partner over tiny things and avoiding my usual sketching group because I feel too stressed and embarrassed to show up. On top of that, I've been avoiding my bills and missing payment deadlines to the point where I almost got a formal eviction warning from my landlord.
Have your stress and mood symptoms been improving as you adjust to the gallery closing, or do they keep getting worse and feel out of proportion to the situation? Two sentences at most.

No, it hasn't improved yet and still feels incredibly overwhelming and out of proportion to how I normally handle things. But I really expect that once I can find a steady part-time job or a new source of income, this level of distress will finally ease up.
Since this stress started, have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
No, I haven't had any thoughts like that at all. Even though the stress is overwhelming, I have never felt like hurting myself or that life isn't worth living.

Have you been able to keep up with your usual responsibilities, or has this stress led to major problems like missing work, neglecting self-care, or withdrawing from people more than you normally would?

Yes, it has definitely caused major problems with my responsibilities and social life. I've been avoiding my bills and missing payment deadlines, which almost got me evicted. I've also been withdrawing from people, especially my sketching group, because I feel too stressed and embarrassed to face anyone right now.
Have you started to feel any better as you adjust to the gallery closing, or do the symptoms keep going without improvement even as time passes?

No, they haven't improved at all and are still ongoing since the gallery closed about a month ago, as the financial stress is still hanging over me. I really expect that once I can land a steady part-time job or find a new income stream, this distress will ease up since it's so tied to this money crunch.
Have your symptoms started to improve at all since the gallery closed, or do they keep going even after the financial stress has eased a bit?

No, they haven't gotten any better because the financial stress hasn't eased up at all yet. I'm still right in the middle of this money crunch, but I really expect things will improve once I can secure a steady part-time job or a new source of income.
Have you noticed any symptoms like feeling very sad or hopeless, losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or trouble sleeping since this stress started?

I have been avoiding things I normally enjoy, like my sketching circles and gallery visits, because they remind me of my stalled career and make me feel too stressed and embarrassed to go. However, I don't feel deeply hopeless or sad in a general sense, and I haven't really had trouble sleeping—it's mostly just the stress and avoiding my hobbies.
Has this stress been caused by one clear life event, and do you expect your symptoms to improve once that situation changes?

Yes, it was definitely triggered by that one clear event of the gallery closing and losing my main source of income about a month ago. I fully expect my symptoms to improve once I can secure a steady part-time job or a new income stream, as this distress is directly tied to my current money crunch.
Have these stress-related symptoms started to improve at all, or have they continued for more than 6 months after the gallery closed?

The gallery actually closed just about a month ago, so it hasn't been six months yet. My symptoms are still ongoing right now, but I expect them to improve once I can find a steady part-time job or a new income stream to relieve this financial pressure.
Have these stress-related symptoms lasted for more than 6 months, or are they still limited to the time since the gallery closed about a month ago?

They are definitely still limited to the month or so since the gallery closed, and they haven't lasted for six months. I fully expect this distress to ease up once I can find a steady job or new income stream, rather than dragging on indefinitely.

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with an adjustment disorder: symptoms began within about 1 month of an identifiable psychosocial stressor (loss of gallery income/closure), are clearly tied to that stressor, cause marked distress and functional impairment (relationship conflict, social withdrawal, missed bills/near eviction), and have not persisted beyond 6 months. Generalized anxiety disorder is less likely because the worry is not present for 6 months and is situation-specific, and a depressive episode is less likely because the patient denies pervasive depressed mood, hopelessness, and major neurovegetative symptoms.
